subject.title: Telegram getUpdates 409 cascade after IPv6→IPv4 transport fallback; rebuild loop self-perpetuates without canceling in-flight long-polls

question: Should OpenClaw solve this broken-IPv6 Telegram getUpdates cascade with polling lifecycle recovery, an opt-in IPv4 startup pin, or both?
rationale: The source path is real and user-visible, but the best durable behavior affects Telegram transport ownership, restart timing, and whether OpenClaw should add another operator network knob.

options.title: Prefer lifecycle recovery plus proof
options.body: Require the polling restart path to abort or destroy the old getUpdates transport and wait or back off enough to avoid Telegram's stale poll slot before opening a new poll, validated against a live broken-IPv6 setup.

options.title: Accept IPv4 opt-in mitigation
options.body: Review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/78438 as an operator escape hatch while accepting that it adds config/env surface and may not solve stale-poll lifecycle generally.

options.title: Keep diagnostics only
options.body: Treat the report as environmental or external-poller driven and keep docs/status guidance without changing transport behavior.

recommendation.title: Prefer lifecycle recovery plus proof
recommendation.body: Require the polling restart path to abort or destroy the old getUpdates transport and wait or back off enough to avoid Telegram's stale poll slot before opening a new poll, validated against a live broken-IPv6 setup.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has recent history on the polling transport lifecycle helper and is the best match for the lifecycle-vs-config direction choice among the related owners.
